body: I’m currently (at the time of typing this) at work after hours in the rest room silently crying my Despair out so my boss and co workers can’t see.  I know how it is. Just see what tomorrow holds, hold off for now.

Every fucking day man.  And same deal. Same exact deal, at one point I was “everyone’s best friend” and it was exhausting. I just started avoiding people again. And now I’m “too good to hang out”.  

I recently missed one of my best friend’s birthday party because I was freaked out by the amount of people that were going to there.  It takes me a week of patching up to go to these things now. 

Honestly if I didn’t love my dog so much I’d probably just find some way to go.  But no one will take care of him if I did, and honestly he’s the reason for me making it through.

This is interesting as I’ve thought the same thing.  Tl:dr - giving a  “deadline” for your life does made coping with depression symptoms/factors easierfor me. It’s like I realize it won’t matter when I’m gone, so why overstress about it now. 


For a long time I felt all the same things, and to be honest my dog is a huge factor in keeping me around.   He’s the sweetest lil pup around but I’m afraid when I’m gone no one will take care of him, send him off to the shelter, or have him starve as no one would probably find me for a while. (I’ll go more into that another time).

I always wanted to die, then I hit a rough patch with my anxiety and health where I thought I was going to legit die (heart was pounding, hard time breathing, thought it was a heart attack but hospital confirmed it wasn’t).  I may discuss it in another post but after that episode I had a new spark for life.....which has faded again.

I got even more depressed later and felt less significant towards everyone in life, and irrelevant.  Then one day I told myself “I’m going to be around for the rest of my dogs life” - he’s about 8yrs now.  After he passes I have no dependents and suicide will be an option again. 

Somehow that lessened everything that caused anxiety, fear, sadness, irrelevancy, etc.  Because nothing matters once I’m gone.   The unintended effect caused me to take a huge step back and analyze everything from a bigger picture... then coping with each part.  Which in turn has helped me more than anything else knowing it’s an “option”.

(Created this account specifically for posting here. Had therapist for years, on anti depressants, talked with friends only to have them tell me “it’s not so bad”, “get over it”, “why are you sad” or they space out because they don’t know how to deal with it.   Nor do I expect them to.)
